chapter: Hopkins, Kelly's Stables and Red Allen
title: Kenny Clarke's Kansas City Six at Kelly's Stables
summary: Ralph Watkins hired him to lead a group with Ike Quebec, Willie Nelson, John Simmons and Monk; Monk and Hawk took over the band after he was drafted.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Okay, Kenny. Now we've got to go back to where we quit last night, which was when you'd left Ella and you went back to Minton's.
So then from Minton's Ralph Watkins at Kelly Stables wanted you to come down.
And then -- so you were heading a group there.
Uh-huh. Kenny Clarke's Kansas City Six.
I don't know why we said Kansas City. I'm from Pittsburgh.
In that group there was Ike Quebec.
Willy Nelson on trumpet. And a wonderful little trumpet player from Newark.
: Did he play with Duke for a while afterwards?
Ike Quebec was a -- he was a very good friend. And he decided that Willy Nelson would be a good running mate for him. So I said okay. Since I'd hired Ike.
So he said, 'Well, I think Willy is a good trumpet player, Kenny, and I think he and I, we have a lot of things in common, and I'd like to work,' so I said, 'Well, get Willy.'
So we had Willy and Ike, John Simmons on bass.
: Yeah. Did he go abroad afterwards?

And we had a piano player from Chicago who had sort of a problem with his family or something like that. So he stayed with us about a couple of weeks and then I got Monk, and Monk was our pianist really, you know, because --
Well, that must have been a fine little group.
Oh, it was fantastic. And Ralph would just pass us all the time and grin, he was so pleased that I knew good musicians.
Yeah. And so that was under your own name.

Yeah. And then after I went into the Army, then Monk and Hawk took over the band. That's when they did those -- Monk and Hawk did those recordings of things, you know. Things like -- well, that led right into that.
Which I was very happy, you know, that they kept things together, you know, that Monk and Hawk became sort of an establishment, you know.
They did quite a few things together,
